decision_titles: Minutes of the September 3, 2026 Regular Meeting
Bid waiver to hire a transitional consultant for Chippanee
plain_text:
ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
Thursday, October 1, 2026, 2026 at 5:00pm 
City Council Chambers, City Hall, 111 N. Main Street & on Zoom 
 
Present:  Mayor Zoppo-Sassu -- Chair, Howard Schmelder -- Vice Chair (Zoom), City 
Council Member Susan Tyler, Commissioners Dave Mills, Jason Paul Sirko, 
Tom Hick, LaQuita Kearney-Gonzales, Louise Provenzano, Marvin (Mickey) 
Goldwasser (Zoom) 
 
Absent:  None 
 
ECD Staff:  Justin Malley - Executive Director, Dr. Dawn Leger - Grants Administrator 
 
Guests: None 
 
Note: City Council Member Tyler called the meeting to order as acting Chair 
while the mayor was in route to attend. 
 
I. Call to Order 
City Council Member Tyler called the Meeting to order at 5:03pm and led all 
present in the Pledge of Allegiance. There was a quorum. 
 
II. Public Participation 
There was no Public Participation. 
 
III. Approval of Minutes 
A. Minutes of the September 3, 2026 Regular Meeting 
The acting Chair called for a motion to approve the Minutes from the September 
3, 2026 meeting. The motion was made by Commissioner Provenzano and was 
seconded by Commissioner Hicks. No edits or amendments were noted. All 
were in favor and the Minutes were accepted into the record. 
 
IV.         Consent Agenda 
A.  Communications 
B.  Economic Development/Grants/Marketing Report 
The acting Chair called for a motion to approve the Consent Agenda. The motion 
was made by Commissioner Goldwasser and was seconded by Vice Chair
Schmelder. No items were called out for discussion. All were in favor and the 
Consent Agenda was accepted into the record. 
 
V.      New Business 
A.  Downtown Update 
Justin Malley spoke regarding next steps in the development of 273 Riverside 
Ave., aka the Sessions Building. The preferred developer, JHM Group, will be 
presenting a purchase and sale agreement to the city. When presented it will be 
reviewed internally. Some elements may need to come before the ECD Board, 
including the tax abatement portion. The timeline on this is encouraging. When 
asked by Vice Chair Schmelder, Justin noted that open windows spaces are 
being covered and the building is currently secure. 
 
Dr. Leger was acknowledged for securing a grant towards Phase I of the required 
environmental work across the street from the Sessions building, aka the former 
Wonder Bread building. Planned demolition requires hazardous building 
material testing. At one time the space was a hardware and/or fertilizer store. 
The Naugatuck Valley Council of Governments (NVCOG) has agreed to fund the 
first piece of the property’s assessment work. 
 
Sei Bella is operating a series of soft opening weekends with a hard launch date 
and hours to be publicized in the coming weeks. Current feedback from patrons 
is very encouraging. Soft launch hours are 4pm to 10pm. 
 
Downtown parking was again as follows: 
• Bristol Health after hours and on weekends 
• the Hope Street garage 
• Municipal parking spaces after hours and on weekend, and 
• along North Main Street and Riverside Avenue 
 
Commissioner Hick expressed his concern about the lack of lighting along the 
path from Tavello on N. Main St. to Iron Horse on Main St. He relayed an 
uncomfortable experience which disturbed visiting relatives as they 
encountered others around the tracks when they were walking the path. 
Discussion followed. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu joined the meeting at 5:17pm.
The mayor noted these economic issues aren’t isolated to Bristol and provided 
information on directed downtown police patrols. She also advised that lights on 
the path are being addressed, and cameras will be put in the parking garage. She 
also noted that the increase in improvements downtown have led to a reduction 
in litter, full housing at Centre Square, more housing being proposed, and a low 
crime rate. The mayor credited Bristol’s social service agencies and the services 
they provide, including to those facing significant economic affordability issues, 
for their part in the process. Discussion followed. 
 
The mayor resumed the meeting as Chair at 5:20pm. 
 
B. Tax Increment Financing Review 
The City’s Public Policy Intern, Nick Carmelich, shared a presentation on the Tax 
Increment Financing Program (TIF) as a review for the Board. Bristol created a 
TIF District in downtown to use future property tax growth to support economic 
development and downtown improvements. The TIF will be part of the JHM 
Group review in the coming month. Discussion followed. 
 
C. “Parade in Reverse” 
A review of the “Parade in Reverse” which was held in previous years and was a 
much-loved event, but hasn’t taken place in several years. Social media interest 
in reviving the “Parade in Reverse” was researched by Kaidyn Sigmund, Intern to 
ECD and the Mayor’s Office, and the response was very positive.  
 
The tentative parade date is Sunday, December 6, 2026 as “The Children’s 
Holiday Parade in Reverse”. The parade path is being outlined including Hope 
Street and into Downtown. Parking and event space would be blocked off in 
front of City Hall, and downtown businesses would be invited to participate and 
partner on the event. 
 
Mum Festival volunteers were asked by the mayor to consider lending their 
expertise and some elements of their canceled signature event to the parade. 
Their involvement would tie the two traditions together and bring families 
downtown. Discussion followed. 
D. Chippanee Update 
Permission for a bid waiver to hire a transitional consultant was approved at a 
Special Board of Finance Meeting earlier that day. The National Golf Foundation
was chosen and will guide the city through both short- and long-term planning. A 
task force of residents interested in the development of the space for the city 
has also been assembled. 
 
The closing is scheduled for November, and the golf course is scheduled to 
open on April 1, 2027. A short-term plan is in progress for November 3, 2026 to 
March 30, 2027. The city is working with existing course vendors with the goal to 
provide access and amenities to the general public as well as existing club 
members. The City is entering into a short-term contract with the existing venue 
vendor with currently booked events planned to proceed as scheduled. 
Marketing will need to be considered. 
 
E. Vaping Moratorium Update 
The Zoning Commission adopted the City Council’s request for the vaping 
moratorium on new businesses for 18 months starting November 3, 2026. The 
moratorium allows time for confirming the guidelines for new and existing 
business standards for operating in Bristol and amongst themselves. A key item 
to tie in are two major state laws which passed in May 2026. Discussion 
followed. 
 
VI.        New Business by Commissioners 
Commissioner Goldwasser thanked the Mayor and the City for their partnership 
with regard to the difficult decision of cancelling the Annual Mum Festival. The 
Mum Festival Committee looks forward to participating in the “Parade in 
Reverse”. 
 
The Commissioner also offered his assistance with marketing the golf course, 
and Commissioner Kearney-Gonzales also referenced her experience owning an 
event planning company. 
 
The following new businesses were noted: 
• Bristol Printing Services (Under New Ownership) – Ribbon cutting 
October 2nd at 11AM 
• Cyriously Hair – Ribbon Cutting October 6th at 11AM 
 
The Code Enforcement Committee is closely monitoring 45, 59 and 81 N. Main 
Street regarding being for sale and maintaining communication to allow for an 
appropriate transition.
VII.       Old Business by Commissioners 
Commissioner Provenzano asked about progress at the former Chic Miller 
location progress. The mayor advised that plans continue to for housing, and 
possibly retail. Work is expected to continue through the winter. Justin Malley 
confirmed for Commissioner Hick that no utilities, including heating, will be 
running or need to be paid for the Sessions Building this winter. 
 
VIII.    Committee Reports 
A. City Council Member Report 
City Council Member Tyler advised of the last two dates for the Bristol Farmers 
Market in October. A Fall Festival will be held in the same location and time (18 
Main St., 10am to 1pm) on November 14, 2026. 
 
A ribbon cutting was held at the new Agave Azul with excellent food and a unique 
feel and energy. 
 
City Council Member Tyler is pleased to report on the continued progress of 
residents being homed and sheltered, and community outreach workers, staff 
and fellow residents bridging gaps left by the closing of Brian’s Angels. St. 
Vincent De Paul’s winter overflow shelter is in its final planning and funding 
stages. The shelter will be in a new, yet to be announced location, and have been 
approved to increase from 20 beds to 25 beds. 
 
The mayor advised that a team of representatives from St. Paul Vincent De Paul, 
Bristol Hospital, Wheeler Health, social service agencies and churches meet 
informally every other week to discuss high priority cases. She reported that one 
previously unhoused resident the group intervened on behalf of is thriving in his 
group home. This team is bringing creative and effective means to help address 
long-term issues. 
 
Housing needs and affordable housing were topics discussed with Gov. Ned 
Lamont when he made a recent drop-in visit to the city. He is committed to the 
housing resources becoming available. Conversations will continue for the city to 
identify and access state resources for those goals. A “Vacancy to Vibrancy” 
concept is being considered where vacant properties are transformed into 
necessary housing.
Commissioner Hick expressed his thanks for the opportunity to have served on 
the ECD Board of Commissions and for the model they provide in service to the 
community. Commissioner Hick has been appointed to the Board of Education 
Committee and formally submitted his letter of resignation to ECD Staff. The 
Board thanked Tom for his contributions over the years and wished him well. 
 
IX.     Adjournment 
With no further business to address, a call was made for a motion to adjourn. The 
motion was made by Commissioner Provenzano and was seconded by 
Commissioner Kearney-Gonzales. All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 
6:05pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary
